Re-checked from first principles:

P = $50,000 borrowed. Monthly rate = APR/12.
For n months, level payment:
Payment = P * r*(1+r)^n / ((1+r)^n -1)
Total interest = n*Payment - P
Total cost = interest + upfront cash fee.

Loan A is dominated by Loan B: same P, same n=36, but
rate_A 8.9% > rate_B 7.9% and fee_A 3% > fee_B 0%.
So cost_A > cost_B necessarily.

Loan C vs A: same rate 8.9%, n=72 vs 36, so much more
interest, fee saving only $1000, so cost_C > cost_A.

Hence B is lowest. Compute value:

Loan B: r = 0.079/12 = 0.0065833333, n=36
(1+r)^36 ≈ 1.266457056
Payment = 50000 * r*(1+r)^36 / ((1+r)^36-1)
 ≈ 50000 * 0.00833750895 / 0.266457056
 ≈ 1564.5127008
Total paid = 36*Payment ≈ 56322.45723
Interest = Total - 50000 ≈ 6322.45723
Fee = 0
Total cost ≈ $6322.46

Loan A check: r=0.089/12=0.0074166667, n=36, fee=1500
(1+r)^36≈1.30475427, Payment≈1587.66070
Interest≈7155.79, cost≈8655.79 > B.

Loan C check: r=0.089/12, n=72, fee=500
(1+r)^72≈1.70238369, Payment≈898.79737
Interest≈14713.41, cost≈15213.41 > B.

Lowest is B at about $6,322.46.
